messages:
Alexa: Heads-up: saw a tail-latency regression on qwen2.5 after yesterday's kernel-selector change. 99th latency up ~35% for seq_len=2048 on dedicated pools. Repro locally.
Mike: Yikes. Any flamegraph or perf trace? :eyes:
Alexa: Pushed a short trace to the thread. Key bit: kernel_selector picks 'autokernel->alibi-path' but it falls back mid-attention to a generic matmul for heads>64. Hot loop shows repeated KV-cache read/write churn.
Alexa: Profiler summary:
```
hot functions:
  attention_autokernel_select()  -> 42%
  generic_matmul()               -> 27%
  kv_cache_fetch_write()         -> 18%
  tokenizer_unicode_normalize()  -> 6%
```
Mike: That fallback sounds like kernel mismatch (head dim vs kv dim). Did the selector mis-detect head layout for qwen2p5 variants?
Yara: We recently enabled ropescale heuristics for qwen2p5 (scale=0.75) to reduce rotary overflow. That changes the indexing math for attention offsets. If autokernel expects ALiBi-style offsets it might pick a different kernel variant.
Sam: Also seeing unusual tokenizer behavior for mixed CJK + latin inputs — tokenization produces longer prefix tokens which increases KV cache entries and evictions. That amplifies the matmul fallback cost.
perf-bot: Alert: Regression detected on dedicated-prod-qwen2p5 pool (latency +33% over 1h). Ticket: PERF-4127.
Mike: Quick experiment: can you force kernel=matmul_fused vs kernel=attention_fused and run the same workload? I want baseline numbers.
Alexa: Ran both. results (seq=2048, batch=1, 8 heads of 128):
  kernel=attention_fused -> p50 180ms p95 360ms p99 420ms
  kernel=matmul_fused    -> p50 210ms p95 450ms p99 560ms
  kernel=legacy (old selector) -> p50 175ms p95 340ms p99 400ms
So legacy beats autokernel->fallthrough.
Yara: That suggests autokernel heuristic wrongly chooses alibi/rope-mixed path and then falls back to generic matmul for some head sizes. Fallback cost >> benefit.
Sam: For the tokenizer angle: mixed-language prompts trigger longer token splits, which means more KV entries and higher probability of eviction. We should check the kvcache eviction policy — it's currently segment-count based, not token-count based. That causes premature eviction of useful prefix.
Mike: Short mitigations: 1) revert autokernel default for qwen2p5 until selector updated, 2) change kvcache eviction to token-count LRU, 3) tighten ropescale->kernel mapping so ropescale variants pick a consistent kernel.
Alexa: Agreed. I'll open a PR reverting default autokernel for qwen2p5 and a follow-up PR with a selector unit test for head/kv dim combos. PRs: https://git.redwood/pr/6312 (revert), https://git.redwood/pr/6313 (selector tests).
Yara: I'll prototype a simple kvcache patch (token-count LRU) and run the stress harness with mixed CJK+latin corpora. If it reduces eviction churn we can ship quick.
Sam: Also add a quick profiling job that runs tokenization traces in CI — fail if average token count per prompt changes >10% after tokenizer changes.
Mike: One more thing: check quantization path. We had an upstream change that changed tensor strides for int8 kernels; that could trigger mismatched kernel choice. If strides differ autokernel may pick a kernel that can't use the packed fused attention, hence fallback.
Alexa: Good catch. I'll add a stride check in the kernel selector and a guard that forces fallback to legacy fused when strides incompatible.
perf-bot: Note: I've scheduled a nightly perf run that will compare current main vs revert branch for qwen2p5 (seq=1024/2048) and post results in #eng-runtime.
Mike: Thanks. Plan: revert today, kvcache patch + selector tests tomorrow, then re-enable autokernel behind an opt-in flag with safety checks. :thumbsup:
Alexa: Thanks team — I'll merge revert after tests pass and paste deploy link here.
Mike: If anyone is free ping me, I'll help with bisecting the autokernel heuristics.
Yara: I'll drop initial kvcache PR by EOD. :coffee:
Alexa: Deploy link: https://deploys.redwood/commit/fead123 (will monitor).
